title: B2+ · L39 — Philosophical discussions
description: Debatir temas abstractos filosoficamente: consider, assume, presuppose, y estructuras para argumentos profundos.

questions.prompt: En un seminario de filosofia se abre debate sobre libre albedrio.
questions.question: 'Let's consider the possibility that X' is used to:
options: Introduce X as a hypothesis for discussion, without endorsing it.
questions.explanation: 'Consider the possibility' = plantear una hipotesis para explorarla, sin adoptarla. Central en debate filosofico maduro. Permite discutir ideas polemicas manteniendo distancia intelectual. Registro: academico-formal, funciona en clase, en debate y en writing. Familia: 'entertain the idea that', 'suppose for a moment that', 'imagine that'. Error hispano: usar 'let's think that X is true' — no es plantear hipotesis, es afirmar. La distincion entre CONSIDER (evaluar) y BELIEVE (aceptar) es la marca del pensamiento filosofico.
examples: Consider the possibility that free will is an illusion — what follows for moral responsibility? → apertura de debate
What if we consider the possibility that AI could, in principle, be conscious? → hipotesis provocadora

questions.prompt: Un ponente desarma la pregunta antes de responderla.
questions.question: 'Presuppose' means:
options: To assume something as true implicitly, before further discussion.
questions.explanation: 'Presuppose' = presuponer, asumir tacitamente. Toda pregunta y toda afirmacion esconden presuposiciones. La clasica 'Have you stopped stealing?' presupone que robabas — no puedes responder sin comprometerte. Central en logica, pragmatica y filosofia del lenguaje. Registro: academico-tecnico. Distincion util: 'assume' (mas neutral) vs 'presuppose' (subraya que se hace TACITAMENTE, sin declararlo). Error hispano: confundir con 'presuposition' (nombre) — el verbo es 'presuppose', el nombre 'presupposition' /priːsʌpəˈzɪʃən/.
examples: That argument presupposes free will exists — but that's precisely what we're trying to establish. → critica logica
The question 'When did progress start?' presupposes there is such a thing as progress. → analisis meta

questions.statement: In philosophical discussion, it's crucial to distinguish between an assertion and its justification.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Distincion central en pensamiento critico. Assertion = la CLAIM (afirmar 'X es verdad'). Justification = el ARGUMENTO que sustenta la claim ('porque Y, Z, W'). Confundirlas es una falacia comun — aceptamos claims sin evaluar los razones que las sustentan. Rigor filosofico basico. Registro: academico-tecnico. Familia conceptual: premise, argument, warrant, evidence. Aplicacion practica: cuando alguien afirma algo, la respuesta madura es 'what's the justification for that?' — no 'yo no lo creo'. Error hispano frecuente: responder a assertions con opinions en vez de con questions sobre la justification.
examples: Assertion: 'X is true.' Justification: 'Because of Y, Z, and W — here's the reasoning...' → estructura logica
Never accept an assertion without asking for the justification behind it. → habito critico

questions.prompt: En un panel academico, quieres proponer una tesis sin sonar dogmatico.
questions.question: Which is a philosophically-appropriate hedge?
options: It seems reasonable to suggest that...
questions.explanation: 'It seems reasonable to suggest that' = hedge triple: 'seems' (apariencia, no certeza) + 'reasonable' (juicio moderado) + 'suggest' (proposicion, no afirmacion). Formula filosofica humilde que reconoce la escasez de verdades absolutas. Registro: academico-filosofico, funciona en papers y en debate oral. Familia escalonada: 'one might argue' (mas hedge), 'it could be argued' (impersonal), 'arguably' (adverbio, muy comun), 'plausibly'. Error hispano cultural: los academicos hispanos a menudo suenan demasiado afirmativos en anglo por transferencia del estilo continental — el ingles filosofico VALORA la humildad epistemica.
examples: It could be argued that consciousness is fundamental to reality itself — a controversial but defensible view. → hedge academico
One might reasonably suppose that morality has evolved rather than been discovered. → proposicion humilde

questions.text: The premise assumes that human reason is the only reliable path to truth — but is that itself a defensible claim?
questions.explanation: Discurso filosofico avanzado. 'Premise', 'reason', 'reliable path', 'defensible claim' — vocabulario tecnico de epistemology. La move retorica clasica: identificar una premisa oculta y cuestionar su justification. Feature de connected speech: 'reliable path' /rɪˈlaɪəbl pæθ/ con /l/ oscura tipica anglo; 'itself a' encadena /ɪtˈselvə/ con weak form del articulo. 'Defensible' /dɪˈfensəbl/ es adjetivo culto (defendible con argumentos). El dash marca pausa reflexiva antes de la pregunta que desmonta.
examples: The argument assumes we can trust our intuitions — a rather big assumption to smuggle in. → critica ironica
The claim rests on a premise that itself deserves scrutiny before we accept the conclusion. → rigor academico

questions.prompt: En un curso de logica se explica un idiom malinterpretado con frecuencia.
questions.question: 'That begs the question' — used strictly / correctly — means:
options: It raises a further, related question.
It assumes what it's trying to prove (circular reasoning).
questions.explanation: 'Beg the question' TECNICAMENTE = razonamiento circular (petitio principii): el argumento asume la conclusion que pretende demostrar. En uso POPULAR (muy extendido) = 'raise a question' (suscitar una pregunta). Puristas filosofos y logicos insisten en el significado tecnico; el uso popular ya es tan comun que muchos dicen que es aceptable. Recomendacion: en contexto academico, uso estricto; en conversacion informal, ambos usos son entendidos. Error hispano: no saber que existe la distincion — es de las 3-4 phrases mas malentendidas del ingles.
examples: Technically: 'God exists because the Bible says so, and the Bible is true because God wrote it' — that begs the question. → circular
Popular use: 'The new policy passed unanimously, which begs the question — what's next?' → suscita pregunta

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino tecnico de filosofia/logica con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Vocabulario tecnico esencial de filosofia y logica formal. Cada termino permite analizar el pensamiento con precision. Base del critical thinking. Distinciones utiles: 'premise' es lo que se ASUME al comenzar; 'assumption' es cualquier cosa dada por supuesta; 'implication' es lo que se SIGUE logicamente; 'argument' NO es discusion emocional sino cadena de razones. 'Fallacy' /ˈfæləsi/ = razonamiento defectuoso con nombre propio (straw man, ad hominem, false dichotomy). Registro: academico-tecnico.
examples: The premise is false, so the conclusion doesn't follow — the argument fails at the root. → analisis logico
That's a straw man fallacy — you're attacking a caricature, not the position I actually hold. → identificacion tecnica

questions.target: If we accept the premise, the conclusion follows logically — but the premise itself is far from settled.
questions.explanation: Estructura filosofica clasica: (1) reconocer la validez interna del argumento — 'the conclusion follows logically'; (2) desmontar la premisa — 'far from settled'. Marca de pensador riguroso: separa la LOGICA de la VERDAD de las premisas. Nivel graduate seminar. Ritmo natural: enfasis en 'accept' y en 'logically', pausa reflexiva tras el dash, tono descendente y firme en 'far from settled'. Contracciones no aplican (registro formal-analitico). Formula transferible a cualquier debate: nunca ataques la conclusion sin evaluar primero la validez logica y la solidez de las premisas por separado.
examples: The logic is sound; the assumption is questionable — which is where the whole thing unravels. → distincion critica
The argument works if we accept X — but why should we? That's the question no one is asking. → giro socratico

questions.prompt: En un debate politico se detecta un truco retorico.
questions.question: 'A false dichotomy' is:
options: Presenting only two options when more exist in reality.
A rhetorical question with no answer.
questions.explanation: 'False dichotomy' (tambien 'false dilemma' o 'either/or fallacy') = falacia que fuerza a elegir entre A o B cuando existen C, D, E. Falacia clasica en debate politico, retorica polarizante y ventas de alta presion. Reconocerla y nombrarla es defensa intelectual. Registro: academico-critico. Estructura tipica: 'Either you're with us or against us' — false, porque hay indiferencia, neutralidad, o apoyo condicionado. Error hispano: aceptar el marco propuesto ('me estas obligando a elegir') en vez de rechazar la dicotomia ('rechazo la premisa de que solo hay dos opciones').
examples: 'You're either with us or against us' — a textbook false dichotomy that erases the middle ground. → analisis politico
'Freedom or security' is often a false dichotomy — societies routinely balance both. → critica de framing

questions.statement: 'Occam's razor' suggests that when multiple explanations exist, the simplest is usually preferable.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Occam's razor (siglo XIV, William of Ockham) = principio de parsimonia. La explicacion con MENOS supuestos es preferible, cuando las opciones explican igualmente bien los datos. Central en ciencia y filosofia analitica. CUIDADO: 'simplest' no significa 'mas facil de entender' sino 'con menos entidades postuladas'. Malinterpretacion comun. Registro: academico-cientifico, comun en journalism cientifico. Familia: 'parsimony', 'the principle of parsimony'. Error hispano: se dice 'Occam' u 'Ockham' — ambas son aceptadas; la pronunciacion mas comun en anglo es /ˈɒkəmz ˈreɪzər/.
examples: Occam's razor suggests fatigue, not a conspiracy, explains the mistake — fewer moving parts. → aplicacion cotidiana
The simplest hypothesis that fits the data is usually the right starting point — Occam's razor in practice. → principio cientifico

questions.prompt: Un profesor de filosofia introduce una tecnica clasica del razonamiento.
questions.question: 'A thought experiment' is:
options: A brain scan or neuroscientific test.
A hypothetical scenario used to explore an idea or intuition.
A form of meditation or mindfulness practice.
questions.explanation: 'Thought experiment' = experimento mental. Escenario hipotetico para probar intuiciones y explorar consecuencias logicas. Herramienta central en filosofia, fisica teorica, y etica. Clasicos: Trolley problem (Foot, Thomson), Schrodinger's cat (fisica cuantica), Chinese room (Searle, mente/AI), Veil of ignorance (Rawls, justicia). Registro: academico-filosofico. Uso practico: te permite aislar variables imposibles de aislar en la realidad. Error hispano: pronunciar como dos palabras separadas — es un compound noun con acento en 'THOUGHT' (/ˈθɔːt ɪkˌsperɪmənt/).
examples: Consider this thought experiment: if consciousness could be copied, would the copy be you? → dilema de identidad
The trolley problem is the classic ethics thought experiment — decades of debate, no clean answer. → referencia canonica

questions.text: There's a tension between individual liberty and collective welfare that no political theory has fully resolved.
questions.explanation: Discurso politico-filosofico maduro. 'Tension' (marcador de dilema no resuelto), 'individual liberty', 'collective welfare', 'political theory' — abstract nouns duros combinados con precision. Reconocer que un problema es IRRESOLUBLE (no solo dificil) es senal de sofisticacion filosofica. Feature de connected speech: 'There's a' encadena /ðɛərzə/ con weak form; 'political theory' /pəˈlɪtɪkl ˈθɪəri/ con /l/ oscura y /θ/ dental. 'Fully resolved' — nota la pausa breve implicita antes.
examples: The tension between freedom and equality is perhaps constitutive of political life itself. → observacion clasica
No system has fully reconciled individual and communal goods — that's not a bug, it's the condition. → reframe filosofico

questions.prompt: Un moderador de debate invita a explorar la posicion contraria.
questions.question: 'What if the opposite were true?' is a philosophical move called:
questions.explanation: 'What if the opposite were true?' = counterfactual thinking. Jugar 'devil's advocate' es asumir DELIBERADAMENTE la posicion contraria para stress-test un argumento. Central en razonamiento maduro y en institutional design (equipos de red-teaming). Registro: academico-analitico. CUIDADO cultural: en anglo profesional 'let me play devil's advocate' es MOVE POSITIVO — muestra rigor. En algunas culturas hispanas puede leerse como buscar pleito. Error hispano frecuente: no entender que subjunctive 'were' (no 'was') es la forma correcta en counterfactuals — 'if the opposite WERE true', no 'was'.
examples: Let me play devil's advocate — what if we're wrong about all of this and the old approach was actually right? → move analitico
Consider the counterfactual: what if nothing had changed? Would we be better off, or just differently off? → pregunta contrafactual

questions.statement: 'Correlation does not imply causation' is a foundational principle in the philosophy of science.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO — fundamental. Dos variables que se mueven juntas no implican relacion causal. Clasico ejemplo: las ventas de helado y los ahogamientos correlacionan, pero no porque uno cause el otro — ambos son causados por el verano. Confusion cotidiana en journalism y en policy debate. Registro: cientifico-analitico. Aplicacion critica: cuando alguien cita una correlacion como prueba de causa, la pregunta madura es 'what's the mechanism? are there confounders?'. Error hispano frecuente: aceptar titulares que confunden correlation con causation ('el cafe causa cancer' cuando el estudio solo mostro correlation).
examples: Correlation is not causation — a critical distinction in any empirical claim. → principio metodologico
Just because A and B move together doesn't mean A caused B — think of confounders and reverse causation. → analisis riguroso

questions.target: One could argue that consciousness is fundamental to reality itself — a bold claim, but not without serious philosophical support.
questions.explanation: Discurso filosofico master. Estructura: 'one could argue' (hedge academico impersonal) + claim ambiciosa + reconocer los stakes ('bold claim') + defender ('not without serious support'). Ritmo natural: enfasis tonico en 'fundamental', pausa reflexiva tras el dash, tono ascendente en 'bold claim' (concediendo), tono descendente y firme en 'serious philosophical support'. Contracciones no aplican (registro academico). Formula de proposicion filosofica madura: hedge + claim + concession + defense. Nivel graduate seminar, TED-Ed, podcast intelectual.
examples: It could be argued that free will is an illusion — a claim with serious defenders in contemporary neuroscience. → hedge + claim + defense
One might contend that morality is discovered, not invented — a controversial but defensible view in metaethics. → proposicion filosofica
